# S2 — Capability decisions read `ModelProfile`, not provider-name strings

## Context / Problem

Two capability decisions are made by string-matching a provider name. `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:51`
`output_mode()` picks `NativeOutput` only when the prefix is in `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS`
(`structured.py:46`, a frozenset of four literal names), and `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:316` attaches prompt-cache
settings only when the resolved string starts with `anthropic`. Both are wrong for Bedrock-hosted Claude, whose
capability flags differ from the direct Anthropic API — the model string would say `bedrock`, so caching would
silently switch off and structured output would silently take the prompted path. PR #121 hit exactly this and
patched it with a `force_prompted: bool` threaded through four call sites.

## Approach

pydantic-ai exposes a per-vendor capability record at `model.profile` (`ModelProfile`). Replace both string
matches with profile reads, and add a rebar-side profile override layer for cases upstream gets wrong or does
not cover — using `ModelProfile` overrides for Bedrock-hosted Anthropic is the documented upstream guidance
precisely because those flags diverge from the direct API.

Concretely: a `capabilities_for(model)` helper in `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] returns a small frozen
record — `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style` (`none`/`anthropic`/`bedrock`), `supports_thinking` —
derived from `model.profile` with rebar overrides applied. `output_mode()` takes that record instead of a model
string; the cache-settings call selects `anthropic_cache_*` vs `bedrock_cache_*` keys from
`prompt_cache_style`. The `thinking` override (prompted mode is the only thinking-compatible choice) is
preserved as-is.

**Alternative rejected:** PR #121's `force_prompted` boolean. It is a per-call-site patch that grows one
argument per capability per provider, and it encodes the answer at the caller rather than at the model — the
next provider needs another boolean threaded through the same four signatures.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` — `capabilities_for()` + the rebar override table.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — `output_mode()` (`:51`) signature change; delete `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` (`:46`).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — `:316` cache gate reads `prompt_cache_style`.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — `_anthropic_cache_settings` (`:39`) generalized or joined by a bedrock sibling.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` (updated).

## Testing

Unit tier for the mapping (pure function over a profile) plus contract tier for the two consumers, since the
defect class is a consumer reading the wrong signal.

- happy path: an Anthropic model yields `prompt_cache_style == "anthropic"` and `output_mode` returns
  `PromptedOutput`; an OpenAI model yields `native_structured_output=True` and `NativeOutput`.
- edge: `thinking=True` forces `PromptedOutput` regardless of profile (existing contract, must not regress).
- failure path: a model whose profile is missing/unknown degrades to the conservative record
  (`native_structured_output=False`, `prompt_cache_style="none"`) rather than raising, and that degradation is
  logged once.
- contrast case: the existing parameterized test at `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`
  (`test_cache_model_settings_attached_only_for_anthropic`) is rewritten to assert by capability rather than by
  provider name, and still shows cache settings absent for a non-caching model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` no longer exists in the tree (`grep -rn _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS src/` is empty)
- [ ] no `force_prompted`-style boolean is added to any signature
- [ ] `output_mode()` accepts a capability record and its tests assert both output modes plus the thinking override
- [ ] an unknown/missing profile produces the conservative record and one WARNING log line, asserted by test
